targets.title: "Overeducation" in the Labour Market
targets.evidence_quote: After presenting data and methods in Section 3, we conduct a thorough re-examination of the results obtained by Sicherman (1991) in Section 4.1.
targets.outcome_quote: The central finding of the present analysis is that overeducated workers have worse career prospects than correctly allocated workers. This is in clear contrast to the results put forward by Sicherman (1991). Note, however, that we were able to replicate the US results with our German data when using Sicherman’s approach. Therefore, the key to understanding the puzzling pattern of results is to be found in a discussion of the validity of the indicators chosen to indicate upward career mobility, and the quality of specification in Sicherman’s model.

targets.title: Career mobility, job match, and overeducation
targets.evidence_quote: In Section 4.3, we extend Robst’s (1995) test for robustness by using an objective, as well as a subjective, measure of training participation.
targets.outcome_quote: Both measures confirm Robst’s findings that overeducated (undereducated) workers indeed receive less (more) training than correctly allocated ones.

reasoning: German sample re-tests Sicherman occupational mobility and Robst training findings. Main critique is invalidity of original occupational mobility indicators despite successful close replication; hence statistically successful but flawed for Sicherman. Robst training result explicitly confirmed. Sicherman and Galor 1990 is a theoretical model rather than an additional empirical target. Full author manuscript dated 12 October 2001 has matching title and both authors and same wage-growth central result as published abstract; version differences remain possible.
